title: /sessions/read discloses effective agent provider and whether MOE_AGENT_COMMAND overrode it
description:
SPIDR grandchild E of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild D (effective provider is whatever spawn actually resolved).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: extend SessionsView so the operator can see which provider is running and that MOE_AGENT_COMMAND overrode the browser setting when it did. Daemon handler apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts (172 lines) plus decoder apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts (SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS currently [concurrency, outcome, readAt, sessions, totals, unreadable]). Nested object preferred, mirroring SessionsConcurrency: e.g. agentProvider: { effective, envOverride } with exact keys at that level.

NOT IN SCOPE: Seats rendering (child 3), spawn argv, command kind, store writes.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` AND `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (decoder lives in apps/control-room; a bare pnpm test covers neither).

Concurrent: task-92d84d38 (DONE) already added concurrency to this read; live-sessions.ts:133 pins ["activeSeats", "configuredAgentLimit"]. Do not regress that.
definitionOfDone: POST /sessions/read success JSON includes the effective provider and whether an env override is in force. A test with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND set and the durable setting saying the other provider asserts both the effective provider AND the override flag. A test with the env unset asserts the override flag is false and the effective provider matches the setting.

live-sessions.ts decodes the new member(s) under exact-key rules. A test that adds an extra key or drops a key on the new nested object (if nested) returns ERROR SESSIONS_RESPONSE_INVALID at CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_SESSIONS. SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS and the daemon SessionsView members stay in lockstep — the existing live-sessions.test.ts source-text pin against sessions-read.ts must stay green.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for either apps/** package.

THE NAMING, which is the substance. Not `effective`. The daemon cannot observe what the wrapper resolved — separate processes — so a member an operator reads as "what is actually running" would be a lie this endpoint has no standing to tell. `configured` carries the claim-limit in the NAME, exactly as `configuredAgentLimit` does three declarations above, and the docblock states the same four facts in the file's own voice: (i) the durable per-project setting IS read from this daemon's store and IS authoritative — the same ledger `project.set_agent_provider` writes and the wrapper reads per spawn; (ii) `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` is read from THIS DAEMON PROCESS'S environment, agreeing with the wrapper only in the `moe up` launched configuration; (iii) what a STANDALONE daemon reports — `envOverride: false` plus whatever its store says, which is what the next `moe up` would resolve; (iv) "Nothing here measures the wrapper."

STATED LIMIT, not papered over: the docblock says in its own paragraph that this read is PROJECT-scoped (`createSessionsReadPort` takes a projectId and no goal), that `configured` is therefore the PROJECT default, and that a per-GOAL override exists in the durable store, outranks the project setting at spawn, and is NOT disclosable here. No goal parameter was invented.

PRECEDENCE IS NOT RE-DERIVED. `agentProviderOf()` calls the orchestrator's own `resolveAgentProvider({ envCommand, settingFor })` with NO goalRef, which walks rungs 1/3/4 (env > project scope `""` > `claude`) — the same function the wrapper spawns through, so the disclosure cannot drift from the spawn. New imports: `agentProviderFact, resolveAgentProvider` from `../orchestrator/agent-provider-resolve.js` and `providerFor` from `../orchestrator/moe-up-credentials.js`. The http -> orchestrator direction is precedented (`http/activation-read.ts:28` already imports `providerFor` from the same module) and introduces no cycle: agent-provider-resolve imports `http/health-read.js` + `http/affordance-contract.js`, neither of which reaches sessions-read.

STEP 2(4) — THE SHAPE DECISION FOR EACH HALF, and why they differ:
- DURABLE SETTING: `readProvider?: (store, projectId) => (goalId) => string | null`, OPTIONAL, defaulted to `agentProviderFact` (the production reader). This is the `readSessions`/`readClaims` shape, NOT the `configuredAgentLimit` shape. :78-83's argument for REQUIRED is that a default would publish a value the daemon was never told and no test could tell it from the real knob — that hazard does not exist here, because THE DEFAULT IS THE PRODUCTION READER ITSELF. The fallback path and the real path are the same code. Required would also have forced an edit to `daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:538`, which is peer-dirty and outside this row's owned paths.
- ENV: read DIRECTLY from `process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"]`, with an optional `envAgentCommand` override detected by `"envAgentCommand" in options` (NOT `??`, so an explicit `undefined`/`null` means "env unset" and does not silently fall through to the real host env — that distinction is what the DoD's unset arm tests). Same reasoning as above: absent means absent, and absent is exactly the fact `envOverride: false` publishes.

TWO CORRECTNESS DECISIONS WORTH NAMING:
1. `envOverride` uses the SAME `present()` rule the resolver applies at rung 1 (`typeof x === "string" && x.trim().length > 0`), so the flag can never claim "the env decided this" about a blank or whitespace `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` that `resolveAgentProvider` ignored. A truthiness check would have desynced the flag from the resolution on `" "`.
2. `configured` publishes `providerFor(command)?.leaf ?? command` — the roster NAME where the command maps to one (`C:\tools\codex.exe` reads `codex`, which is what an operator beside the pause banner needs), and the raw value VERBATIM where it does not. Deliberately NOT `pauseProviderOf`, which collapses an unrecognised command to `"claude"`: that collapse is correct for pause-LEDGER keying (its docblock says so) and wrong for a disclosure, where it would show an operator a provider nobody configured. Measured at agent-provider-store.ts:63 — `readState` refuses the whole read when a stored provider is off `KNOWN_PROVIDERS`, so an off-roster DURABLE value resolves to `"claude"`; the reachable off-roster vector is the unvalidated ENV, and that is the one this rule protects.

TESTS, BOTH SIDES OF THE WIRE.

(1) DAEMON — `apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.test.ts` 193 -> 325 lines. NINE arms in a new describe, all asserting THE JSON THE HANDLER RETURNS: a `body()` helper builds the real port and drives it through `handleSessionsReadRequest`, unwrapping the REPLY. The authenticator fixture's principal is `proj-0001` while the real store is `project-1`, so the port is relabelled with `{ ...port, boundProjectId: "proj-0001" }` — the same idiom the existing project-mismatch arm at :90 uses, and the `readSessions` closure is untouched by it.

THE DURABLE HALF IS DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL STORE, not a double: `storeSet(provider)` writes with the production `setAgentProvider` into `openStore()` and NO `readProvider` is injected, so every value comes back through the port's DEFAULT `agentProviderFact` -> `readAgentProvider` over real sqlite. A `readProvider` never wired to production could not pass these arms.

DoD-1's two arms are a PAIR over one store, which is what makes them non-vacuous:
- ENV SET + durable setting naming THE OTHER provider: store says `codex`, env says `claude` -> `{ configured: "claude", envOverride: true }`. Both the effective provider AND the flag.
- ENV UNSET, same setting -> `{ configured: "codex", envOverride: false }`. Flag false AND the provider equals the setting. Same store, two envs, two different answers, so neither member can be a constant.
Seven more: no-setting-and-no-env -> claude; env as a PATH to a known provider (`C:\tools\codex.exe` and `/usr/local/bin/codex`) -> `codex`, the roster NAME not the path; BLANK env (`""`, `"   "`, `"\t"`) -> `envOverride: false` and the setting's value (the arm that kills a truthiness check on the daemon side — a `!x` guard would claim the env decided a value `resolveAgentProvider` ignored); the env default taken from THIS PROCESS when `envAgentCommand` is not passed (sets and restores `process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"]` in a finally, asserting BOTH directions — this is the arm proving the default is the live env, the analogue of the composition-site pin above it); an unreadable durable read degrading to `claude` with the frame still SESSIONS rather than wedging; and a regression arm holding `concurrency` at `{ activeSeats: 0, configuredAgentLimit: 6 }` plus the refusal's exact three keys.

THE THIRD ARM (off-roster) FOUND A REAL DISAGREEMENT AND I CORRECTED THE TEST, NOT THE PRODUCTION CODE. I first asserted `/usr/local/bin/gemini` -> `configured: "gemini"`. It went RED: `expected { configured: 'gemini' } ... received "/usr/local/bin/gemini"`. The implementation was right and my expectation was wrong — `providerFor` returns undefined off-roster, so `?? command` publishes the raw value, exactly as the member's own docblock already said ("verbatim where it does not"). PINNED DECISION, now stated in both the test and an expanded docblock: a KNOWN command publishes the roster NAME (the identity the pause ledger and banner share); an UNKNOWN command publishes the configured value EXACTLY AS IT STANDS, full path included. Not collapsed to `claude` (what `pauseProviderOf` deliberately does for ledger keying, and what would show an operator a provider nobody configured), and not reduced to a basename either (that manufactures a provider identity that does not exist — `gemini` beside a roster of ["claude","codex"] reads as a provider the daemon knows). THE FILE THIS ROW EDITS ALREADY DOCUMENTS ITS CENTRAL PROBLEM. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 4 files, no new files, no split.

The row's proposed shape (`agentProvider: { effective, envOverride }`, nested, mirroring `SessionsConcurrency`) measured correct and the plan keeps it. What the description leaves open is the **naming**, and that is the substance here.

## The daemon cannot observe what the wrapper resolved

`sessions-read.ts:29-35`, three lines above where this member goes, on `configuredAgentLimit`:

> "CONFIGURED, never observed… The daemon and the wrapper are **separate processes**; `moe up` spawns both from one child environment, so in the launched configuration they agree. A daemon started standalone, or beside a wrapper launched separately with a different value, reports a limit no wrapper is honouring. **Nothing here measures the wrapper.**"

`MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` read inside the daemon is the **daemon's** env. A member called bare `effective` reads to an operator as "what is actually running" — which this endpoint cannot know. The plan requires the name and docblock to carry that limit exactly as `configuredAgentLimit` does. That is the file's own precedent, not an invention.

Note the split in what *is* knowable: the durable project setting is genuinely read from the store and is authoritative; the env override is only the daemon's own environment. The docblock has to say which half is which.

## A second limit, stated rather than papered

`createSessionsReadPort` destructures `{ projectId, store }` and never takes a goal — the read is **project-scoped**. So this member can disclose the project default plus the env override, but **not** a per-goal override, which grandchild C's store does support. The plan forbids adding a goal parameter to a project-scoped read to reach it, and requires the limit be stated in the completion record.

## The member name is constrained by a regex in another package's test

`live-sessions.test.ts:63-75` reads `sessions-read.ts` **as source text** (the control room must never import apps/daemon), then collects members with:

```
/^ {2}readonly (?<name>[A-Za-z]+)[?]?:/gmu
```

Letters only, anchored at two-space indent. A name with a digit or underscore, or a member nested a level deeper, is **invisible to the pin** — which then passes while the two rosters silently disagree. Not a red; a hole. `agentProvider` is fine.

## The failure mode is a blank screen, not a red test

`SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS` is exact-arity (`exactDataRecord` at :129). A daemon member without its decoder key makes the whole frame decode as `SESSIONS_RESPONSE_INVALID` — the constant's own docblock says it "does not degrade the Seats screen, it **BLANKS** it". That is why this is a same-commit rule, and drill (i) proves both directions of it.

## Two smaller things the plan pins

- **A truthiness check on the override flag** would admit any non-empty string and pass every happy-path arm. The file's own `typeof record.unreadable !== "boolean"` at :130 is the model; drill (iii) proves the guard is real.
- **`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is mandatory.** Two of the four files live in apps/control-room, and no other gate sees them — not root `pnpm test` (no `apps/**` in the include), not `pnpm typecheck` (runtime value checks), not the daemon leg.
